text.p: ValuJet Inc said it has realigned its management structure and named D. Joseph Corr president and chief executive of ValuJet Airlines effective November 6.
Corr has previously served as chairman and chief executive at Continental Airlines and president and vice chairman of Trans World Airlines.

The company also named ValuJet Airlines chairman and chief executive Robert Priddy as chairman and CEO of the holding company, ValuJet Inc. It said Priddy will now devote his full time to his new positions at the holding company.
The company said Lewis Jordan will assume the position of chairman of the board of the airline and will retain his position at the holding company as president and chief operating officer.
ValuJet restructured to make ValuJet Airline a wholly owned unit of ValuJet Inc in October 1995.

In September, the Association of Flight Attendants union filed a request to keep ValuJet grounded, requesting that the U.S. Department of Transportation rule the airline was unfit to operate as long as Priddy and Jordan remained in charge.
A U.S. appeals court later rejected the union's request and the airline resumed flights September 30.

In June, ValuJet flights were suspended after a Federal Aviation Administration review found serious deficiencies in its operations, following the May 11 crash of flight 592 in the Florida Everglades, in which all 110 people on board were killed.
"These organizational changes add significant strength to an already strong airline team and facilitate development of other holding company interest," Priddy said.
"Joe Corr, in his new position, will provide excellent leadership in taking ValuJet Airlines to the next level of operational excellence as we continue our development and growth," said Jordan.
